title: NY State Senate · District 20
area: Central Brooklyn (Crown Heights, Flatbush, Park Slope, Prospect-Lefferts Gardens, East Flatbush)

context.text: Zellnor Myrie is unopposed on the November 3 general-election ballot. The Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were both canceled because he had no primary opponent.

Myrie ran for Mayor of New York City in the 2025 Democratic primary, placing sixth, and campaigned on increasing citywide housing supply by loosening zoning rules; he did not advance and returned to seeking re-election to his Senate seat.

candidates.name: Zellnor Myrie
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated without a primary opponent; running unopposed in the general election
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 20 (since January 2019)

summary.text: Zellnor Myrie is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party state senator for District 20, first elected in 2018. He chairs the Senate Codes Committee and is running unopposed for a fourth term after an unsuccessful 2025 run for New York City Mayor.

background.text: Graduated from Brooklyn Technical High School, then earned a B.A. in Communications and an M.A. in Urban Studies from Fordham University and a J.D. from Cornell Law School, where he served as student government president.
His mother immigrated from Costa Rica; he has said this shaped his commitment to public service.
Worked as legislative director for New York City Council Member Fernando Cabrera and later as an attorney at the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell before his 2018 election.
Elected to the State Senate in 2018, defeating incumbent Jesse Hamilton.
Chairs the Senate Codes Committee in the 2025-2026 session; previously chaired the Elections Committee (2019-2022).

priorities.text: Gun violence prevention and accountability for the gun industry
Criminal justice reform, including easing the path to challenge wrongful convictions
priorities.quote: In New York, it's far too easy to be wrongfully convicted and far too difficult to clear your name.

priorities.text: Accountability for federal agents who violate New Yorkers' constitutional rights
priorities.quote: New York won't change ours either: we will always stand up to defend our communities.

positions.summary: Sponsored the New York Bivens Act, signed by Governor Hochul in May 2026, which holds federal agents civilly liable for constitutional-rights violations; issued a statement after ICE shootings in Texas and Maine defending New York's accountability law.
positions.quote: This year New York passed strong laws to hold agents accountable when they violate our constitutional rights.

positions.summary: Authored New York's first-in-the-nation law making illegal gun sales a public nuisance exposing manufacturers to liability (2021), and authored legislation declaring gun violence a public health crisis.

According to his official Senate biography, authored tenant-protection legislation described as among New York's strongest affordable-housing and tenant-protection laws in a generation, including the 2019 Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act.
Ran for Mayor in 2025 on a platform of increasing New York City's housing supply by 700,000 homes through loosened zoning rules in areas with stringent restrictions.

Voted yes on S7898-A, requiring certain state construction contracts to include siting of renewable energy systems, energy storage systems, or major electric transmission facilities; passed the Senate 39-21.

record.text: Sponsored the Challenging Wrongful Convictions Act, which the Senate passed in June 2026; the bill would let defendants seek to overturn convictions based on since-decriminalized conduct or on withheld evidence, inadequate counsel, new forensic findings, or unlawful searches.
Sponsored the New York Bivens Act, which Governor Hochul signed into law in May 2026, creating a state civil-rights cause of action against federal agents for constitutional violations.
Authored a 2021 state law making illegal firearm sales a public nuisance, exposing gun manufacturers to civil liability; the first law of its kind in the nation.
Authored the John R. Lewis New York Voting Rights Act, described by his official biography as the strongest state-level voting rights law in the country.
Voted yes on S7898-A (renewable-energy and energy-storage siting requirements for state construction contracts), which passed the Senate 39-21 on June 1, 2026.
Chairs the Senate Codes Committee in the 2025-2026 session.

researchNotes: Myrie has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and his 2026 campaign website was a placeholder under construction at the time of research, so priorities and positions here are drawn from his official Senate record, press releases, and his 2025 mayoral platform (housing) rather than a current campaign platform.
